name: कांगड़ी लोक
tagline: Lower Himachal. Karnail Rana and the Kangra valley.

tracks.title: Saile Simble Ni Maaye
tracks.note: Karnail Rana has recorded well over a thousand songs across some 250 albums and is the reason Kangri folk kept a mass audience through the cassette and CD eras. He is widely called the Lok Ratna of Himachal.

tracks.title: Adhi Raati Kuku Bolda
tracks.note: The cuckoo calling at midnight is one of the oldest images in Pahari song — a bird heard but not seen, standing in for someone absent.

glossary.meaning: the cuckoo, whose call marks spring and, in song, longing

tracks.title: Mandran Ch Hove Meri Maa
tracks.note: Kangra’s folk and devotional repertoires are not cleanly separable — the same singers, the same melodies, and often the same fairs.

glossary.meaning: fair one — a common way of addressing a woman in song

tracks.title: Hansi Hansi Poochdi Wo Rani Rukmani
tracks.note: A narrative song built on the Rukmini story. Long-form storytelling like this is the older layer of the repertoire, from before songs were cut to a three-minute length.

tracks.title: Kangri Mashup
tracks.note: A run through several Kangri melodies in one take — a useful thing to hear early, because it shows how much of the repertoire shares a common backbone.

tracks.title: Zindagi Sohni Aee
tracks.note: Kangri shades into Dogri as you move west towards Jammu, and singers on that border move between the two without much ceremony.

glossary.meaning: beloved — the standard term of endearment in Kangri and Gaddi song
